title: Video 02 — six hooks, one tutorial · organic 9:16

safeBox.note: Organic, not paid. TikTok's own chrome leaves 211 px at the top and 422 at the bottom of a 1080 x 1920 frame, so anything that must be read sits between y 211 and 1498. If any of the six is ever run as a paid unit, `kind` becomes `paid`, y1 becomes 1128, and every title moves up with it because nothing is positioned by hand.

hooks.type: outcome showcase — the payoff is the opening frame
hooks.title: these captions were made on a phone
hooks.vo: these captions were made on a phone.

hooks.title: airplane mode on. can it still caption?
hooks.segmentsNote: The tile flips to On at 4.4 s of toggle.mp4, read off frames at 0.3 s steps, so the first segment starts a second before it.

hooks.title: most caption apps bill you monthly. this one bills you once.
hooks.vo: most caption apps bill you every month. this one, once.

hooks.type: demonstration of the one thing nobody else does
hooks.hitsNote: Where in these three seconds the loud word takes the frame: the export from 13.0 s reads 'Then ask for 20%' and the box lands on the yellow 20% at 14.0 s. Read off out/exp-sheet.png (two frames a second) and not guessed; if the export is remade, read it again.
hooks.title: it hears which word you leaned on
hooks.vo: it hears which word you leaned on.

hooks.type: claim-first — three statements, not a list
hooks.title: no account. no upload. no server.
hooks.vo: no account. no upload. no server.

hooks.title: nine caption styles. all animating your own words.

beats.title: pick a video

beats.what: Processing — 'Transcribing' with the aeroplane in the phone's own status bar, ringed — and the transcript landing in the editor
beats.title: it transcribes on the phone. nothing is uploaded.
beats.vo: it transcribes on the phone. nothing is uploaded.
beats.segmentsNote: A taller band at a smaller scale, because the Processing screen's 'Transcribing' line sits at y 1440 and the aeroplane it is being ringed against sits at y 61 — a 1180 px band cannot hold both.

beats.what: The editor playing: captions on the stage, the transcript under it, the loud words already bold
beats.title: timed to the word. the loud one gets big.
beats.vo: timed to the word. the loud one gets big.

beats.what: The '1 to check' chip opens the flagged word; one tap and the chip is gone
beats.title: it flags what to check. one tap to fix.
beats.vo: it flags what to check. one tap to fix.

beats.what: The timing sheet: a handle dragged on the waveform, the neighbour following
beats.title: nudge any word. the rest stays put.
beats.vo: nudge any word. the rest stays put.

beats.what: The style sheet: presets tapped, the scroll past six, the hue strip dragged
beats.title: nine looks. your colour, your size, your position.
beats.vo: nine looks. your colour, your size, your position.

beats.title: teach it your words once

beats.what: Export → Save to gallery → the progress bar, then a cut to Saved: the tick, Share, and the feedback card
beats.title: export in seconds. share anywhere.
beats.segmentsNote: The first band is the bottom of the Export screen — the size line, Save to gallery, and the progress bar that replaces it — not the preview, which is a video the viewer has just watched three beats of.

beats.what: The app's own exported file, full frame, the name and the store line over it — a running shot, not a card

export.what: A real Wordburn export of the demo clip. 1080 x 1920, 30 fps, captions burned in by the app's own burn-in module. Pulled off the emulator by ../pipeline/pull-export.mjs after the `saving` shot made it.

checks.note: What ../pipeline/selfcheck.mjs expects on disk after each phase. Every tutorial file is one hook (hookSec) followed by the body.
